tools.name: ping
tools.description: Liveness check. Returns 'pong' to confirm the WeftCut MCP server is reachable.

inputSchema.description: Empty arg shape for tools that take no parameters. The dispatch table deserializes `{}` (or any object) into this; `schemars` advertises it as an empty object schema.
inputSchema.title: EmptyArgs

tools.name: begin_agent_session
tools.description: Enter agent mode: flip the human's UI to a simplified preview / scrub / record-only layout while the agent makes changes. `reason` is a short free-text label shown in the record panel header (e.g. 'cutting filler words'). Creates an automatic checkpoint named 'Pre-agent: {reason}' so the human can revert the entire session in one click. Calling this while already in agent mode replaces the session. The human exits via the UI; there is no end_agent_session tool.

reason.description: Short free-text label shown in the human's record-panel header while the session is active. Examples: "cutting filler words", "applying transcribe + auto-cut pass". Required, non-empty.

tools.name: add_track
tools.description: Add a new track to the project. Returns the new track id as a UUID string. Tracks are kind-agnostic — any layer kind can be placed on any track.

tools.name: remove_track
tools.description: Remove a track. Rejects if the track has layers unless force=true. Default A roll / B roll tracks cannot be removed.

force.description: If true, deletes the track even if it has layers. Default false.

tools.name: move_track
tools.description: Move a track to a different z-order position. 0 = bottom of stack. Position must be < current track count.

new_position.description: Target index in the tracks vector. Must be < current track count.

tools.name: add_color_layer
tools.description: Add a solid-color layer to a track. Returns the new layer id. `t_start_us` and `t_end_us` are timeline microseconds (start inclusive, end exclusive). Layer cannot overlap existing layers on the same track.

height.description: Defaults to composition height when omitted.

width.description: Defaults to composition width when omitted.

tools.name: add_video_layer
tools.description: Add a video clip layer pulling a slice of an imported media item onto a track. `src_in_us`/`src_out_us` are the in/out points within the source media. `t_start_us`/`t_end_us` are where the clip lives on the timeline. The two ranges should be the same length unless `speed` is later changed. When the source media has an audio stream and the project's `auto_pair_audio_on_import` setting is on (default), this also creates a paired Audio layer on an audio track at the same time bounds and groups the two so they move/trim/split together. Returns either the video layer id (legacy mode) or `{ video_layer_id, audio_layer_id, group_id }` when a pair was created.

tools.name: apply_subtitles
tools.description: Import a subtitle document (SRT/VTT/ASS) as a caption track of editable Text layers. Cue timings come from the body. `format` is sniffed when omitted. Advanced ASS styling (karaoke, drawings) is simplified. Returns the new caption track id.

body.description: Subtitle document body (SRT, ASS, or VTT).

format.description: 'srt', 'ass', or 'vtt'. Sniffed from body when omitted.

t_end_us.description: IGNORED — cue timings come from the body, not the timeline envelope. Kept for wire-schema stability; do not remove.

t_start_us.description: IGNORED — cue timings come from the body, not the timeline envelope. Kept for wire-schema stability; do not remove.

track_id.description: IGNORED — a caption import always creates its own Caption-role track. Kept for wire-schema stability; do not remove.

tools.name: detect_silences
tools.description: Find silent regions in a VideoClip or Audio layer using the pre-computed waveform. Walks the layer's peaks file (binary VPEAKS at 100 peaks/sec) and returns timeline-absolute ranges where every peak stays below `threshold_amp` for at least `min_silence_us` microseconds. Defaults: `threshold_amp=0.02` (-34 dBFS), `min_silence_us=500000` (0.5s). Use the returned ranges to feed `split_layer` + `delete_layer` and produce a tighter cut. Returns `[{ t_start_us, t_end_us }, ...]` sorted by t_start_us. Errors with `NotReady` if the waveform job hasn't finished yet — wait for a `media:job_complete` event with `kind=waveform` and retry.

layer_id.description: Target VideoClip or Audio layer id.

min_silence_us.description: Minimum contiguous silence duration (microseconds) to surface. Default 500000 (0.5 seconds).

threshold_amp.description: Peak amplitude threshold in [0.0, 1.0]. Anything strictly below this counts as silence. Default 0.02 (≈ -34 dBFS).

tools.name: update_layer
tools.description: Update a layer's envelope (label, time range, enabled, locked). Only fields you set are applied. Time range changes go through validation.

LayerPatch.description: Partial update for a layer's envelope. Only `Some(_)` fields are applied. `params_patch` carries kind-specific edits; the property panel sends one of the variant patches so the actor can sanity-check the kind matches.

tools.name: update_layer_params
tools.description: Update a layer's kind-specific params. The patch is tagged with `kind` ('Text' | 'VideoClip' | 'ImageOverlay' | 'Color' | 'Audio') and must match the layer's kind. Audio fields take real effect in both preview and export: `gain_db` (dB; this patch sets a STATIC value, replacing any existing keyframes on the track), `pan` (-1..1 equal-power, same static-replace semantics), `fade_in_us`/`fade_out_us` (linear edge fades), `mute`, and `role` (one of dialogue/music/sfx/voiceover) to reassign the clip's mixing role.

AudioRole.description: Fixed v1 role set. Custom / sub-roles are deferred. Kebab-case on the wire (matches `TrackRole`'s convention and the TS `AudioRole` union).

LayerParamsPatch.description:
Kind-tagged partial update for a layer's `params`. Fields are scalar so the UI can drive them with simple inputs; the actor lifts them to `Animated::Static(...)` where the underlying shape is animated.

Limitation: applying a static-value patch to a keyframed field overwrites the keyframe track. Acceptable for the MVP property panel where keyframes are not yet user-editable; revisit when the keyframe UI lands.

motif_id.description: Retarget the layer to a different Motif id (Edit-in-place: swap the selected layer onto a working draft; Discard: swap it back). Paired with `motif_version` so the seen-at marker matches the new target.

props.description: Props to merge into the layer's existing `props` map, FIELD-WISE — each key present here overwrites that key, all other keys are left intact. (Replacing the whole map would let a stale debounced commit clobber a concurrent edit; merge can't delete keys, which is fine — the schema keys are fixed at insert time.) No schema validation here: the actor has no motif-registry access, and props were already validated against the manifest's `props_schema` at `add_motif`.

tools.name: move_layer
tools.description: Move a layer to a different track and/or start time. The end time shifts by the same delta. Cross-track moves are validated against the destination's existing layers — overlap rejects with structured options.

escape_group.description: `docs/groups.md` — when the moved layer is in a group and `escape_group` is `false` or omitted, every group member shifts in time by the same delta. Pass `true` to move only this layer.

tools.name: split_layer
tools.description: Split a layer into two halves at the given timeline microsecond. Returns {left, right} layer ids. `at_t_us` must be strictly between the layer's t_start_us and t_end_us. For media-bearing layers (VideoClip, Audio) the source offsets are adjusted at speed=1 — variable speed support is deferred.

escape_group.description: `docs/groups.md` — when the split layer is in a group and `escape_group` is `false` or omitted, every group member spanning `at_t_us` is also split there (all halves stay in the same group). Pass `true` to split only this layer.

tools.name: delete_layer
tools.description: Delete a layer. When the project setting `auto_delete_empty_tracks` is on (default) and this empties a non-reserved, unlocked track, the track is deleted in the same history entry (one undo restores both). A/B-roll and other role-stamped tracks always stay.

tools.name: trim_layer
tools.description: Trim one edge of a layer's timeline range. `edge` is 'in' (t_start) or 'out' (t_end). For media-bearing layers the corresponding src bound (src_in_us or src_out_us) moves by the same delta; over-trimming past the source bound is clamped. When the layer is in a group and `escape_group` is false (default), every group member whose corresponding edge sits at the same t as the trimmed edge is moved by the same delta, clamped to the tightest aligned member's bounds. Pass `escape_group=true` to trim only this layer. See `docs/groups.md`.

escape_group.description: `docs/groups.md` — when the trimmed layer is in a group and `escape_group` is false or omitted, aligned-edge coupling fans the trim out to other members whose corresponding edge sits at the same time. Pass `true` to trim only this layer.

tools.name: groups_list
tools.description: List every group in the project. Each entry has `id`, optional `label`, and the set of member `layer_ids`. Empty array when no groups exist. Membership is flat — a layer is in at most one group.

inputSchema.description: Empty arg shape for tools that take no parameters. The dispatch table deserializes `{}` (or any object) into this; `schemars` advertises it as an empty object schema.
inputSchema.title: EmptyArgs

tools.name: groups_get
tools.description: Read a single group by id. Returns `{ id, label, layer_ids }` or NotFound.

tools.name: groups_create
tools.description: Create a new group from >=2 distinct layer ids. Optional `label`. If any layer is already in another group, the op fails unless `reassign=true`, which removes them from their prior group(s) first (auto-dissolving any group that falls below 2 members). Returns the new group id.

reassign.description: When any layer is already in another group, `reassign=true` removes it from its prior group first (auto-dissolving if needed). When false or omitted, the op rejects with `LayerAlreadyGrouped`.

tools.name: groups_dissolve
tools.description: Dissolve (delete) a group. The member layers themselves are not deleted.

tools.name: groups_add_members
tools.description: Add member layers to an existing group. Same reassign semantics as groups_create.

tools.name: groups_remove_members
tools.description: Remove member layers from a group. If the remaining membership falls below 2, the group auto-dissolves.

tools.name: groups_rename
tools.description: Update a group's label. Pass `label: null` to clear it.

tools.name: duplicate_layer
tools.description: Duplicate a layer with a time offset. The copy is inserted on the same track. Returns the new layer id. The composition duration extends if needed.

tools.name: get_param_track
tools.description: Read a layer param's animation track, flattened for editing. Returns {"mode":"Static","value":n} or {"mode":"Keyframed","keyframes":[{id, t_us, t_local_us, value, interp}]}. `t_us` is timeline-absolute; `t_local_us` is layer-local (the stored base). Use this to discover keyframe ids before editing.

tools.name: set_keyframe
tools.description: Insert or update a keyframe on a layer param. `t_us` is timeline-absolute. A Static track is lifted to Keyframed. An existing key at the same frame is updated in place. `interp` (optional) sets the easing for the segment leaving this key (e.g. {"kind":"Linear"}, {"kind":"EaseIn"}, {"kind":"Bezier","p1":[x,y],"p2":[x,y]}); omit to inherit the preceding key's easing (or Linear).

tools.name: remove_keyframe
tools.description: Remove a keyframe by id from a layer param. Get the id from get_param_track. When it was the last key, the track collapses to Static holding that key's value.

tools.name: retime_keyframe
tools.description: Move a keyframe to a new timeline-absolute time. The track re-sorts.

tools.name: set_keyframe_easing
tools.description: Set the easing of the segment leaving a keyframe. `interp`: {"kind":"Hold"} | {"kind":"Linear"} | {"kind":"EaseIn"} | {"kind":"EaseOut"} | {"kind":"Bezier","p1":[x,y],"p2":[x,y]}.

tools.name: smooth_keyframes
tools.description: Bake monotone (no-overshoot) smooth tangents. With `keyframe_id`, smooths that one key; without it, smooths the whole track.

tools.name: clear_keyframes
tools.description: Collapse a param's animation back to a single Static value. `value` (optional) is the value to hold; when omitted, defaults to the first keyframe's value. No-op on an already-Static track.

tools.name: set_param_track
tools.description: Low-level: replace a layer param's whole animation track. `track` is an AnimTrack<f64>: {"mode":"Static","value":n} or {"mode":"Keyframed","value":[{id, t_us, value, interp}]} with keyframe `t_us` timeline-absolute. Use the granular tools (set_keyframe etc.) unless you need bulk authoring.

tools.name: add_effect
tools.description: Add an effect to a layer's chain (appended to the end of the chain, applied last). `kind` is the catalog key (v1: "blur"). Returns the new effect id. The effect is created with no params set; use update_effect to set a static value first, then set_keyframe to keyframe it.

kind.description: Catalog key for the effect (v1: `"blur"`). Rust does not validate the key; the renderer rejects unknown kinds at render time.

layer_id.description: UUID of the layer to attach the effect to.

tools.name: update_effect
tools.description: Update an effect: patch is `{ enabled?, params? }` where params is `{ paramKey: { "mode": "Static", "value": <number> } }` (v1 params are scalar). For keyframed params use set_keyframe with param_key "effects[<effect_id>].params[<key>]".

effect_id.description: UUID of the effect to update.

layer_id.description: UUID of the layer that owns the effect.

patch.description: Partial update: `{ enabled?, params? }`. `params` is a map of param key to `Animated<f64>`: `{ "mode": "Static", "value": <number> }` (v1).

tools.name: move_effect
tools.description: Reorder an effect within its layer's chain. new_index is 0-based; 0 = first applied. Must be < effect count.

effect_id.description: UUID of the effect to reorder.

layer_id.description: UUID of the layer that owns the effect.

new_index.description: 0-based destination index (0 = applied first). Must be < effect count.

tools.name: remove_effect
tools.description: Remove an effect from a layer by id.

effect_id.description: UUID of the effect to delete.

layer_id.description: UUID of the layer that owns the effect.

tools.name: set_composition
tools.description: Update composition envelope (canvas size, fps, sample rate, channels, color space, background, duration). Only fields you set are applied. Width/height must be positive; fps denominator must be non-zero. Setting `duration_us` pins the composition duration — subsequent layer edits will no longer auto-fit it (except an overflow guard if a layer extends past the pinned value). Use `fit_composition_to_layers` to clear the pin and snap duration back to the layer high-water mark.

CompositionPatch.description: Partial update for the composition envelope. Only `Some(_)` fields apply.

Rational.description: Frame rate as an exact rational. `30000/1001` ≠ `29.97`, and ffmpeg cares.

tools.name: fit_composition_to_layers
tools.description: Clear the composition's duration pin and set `duration_us` to `max(layer.t_end_us)`. The inverse of `set_composition { duration_us }`: that pins, this unpins. After this call, subsequent layer edits track duration in both directions (grow on adds, shrink on deletes/inward trims).

inputSchema.description: Empty arg shape for tools that take no parameters. The dispatch table deserializes `{}` (or any object) into this; `schemars` advertises it as an empty object schema.
inputSchema.title: EmptyArgs

tools.name: add_marker
tools.description: Add a marker (point or region) to the timeline. Returns the new marker id. Set `end_t_us` to make it a region marker.

end_t_us.description: Set to make this a region marker.

tools.name: update_marker
tools.description: Update a marker. Setting `t_us` re-sorts the marker list.

MarkerPatch.description: Partial update for a marker. Only `Some(_)` fields apply. Setting `end_t_us` to `Some(None)` is impossible through this shape; clearing the region must round-trip through `remove_marker` + `add_marker`.

tools.name: remove_marker
tools.description: Remove a marker.

tools.name: import_media
tools.description: Import a media file from an absolute path. Hashes the file (blake3) and probes metadata via ffprobe when installed. Returns the new media id.

path.description: Absolute path to a video / audio / image / subtitle file the host can read.

tools.name: remove_media
tools.description: Remove a media item. Rejects if any layer references it unless force=true. With force=true, also deletes the referencing layers in one atomic commit.

force.description: If true, also deletes layers that reference this media. Default false.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undo the most recent edit (linear history). Errors with NothingToUndo at the origin. Only timeline edits (layers, tracks, markers, transitions, composition duration, and cascade-deleting media removals) record onto the undo stack. The following sit OUTSIDE it and are unaffected by undo: media imports and removals of unreferenced media, canvas setup changes (width/height/fps/sample_rate/channels/color_space/background), and loading or creating a project (which resets history).

inputSchema.description: Empty arg shape for tools that take no parameters. The dispatch table deserializes `{}` (or any object) into this; `schemars` advertises it as an empty object schema.
inputSchema.title: EmptyArgs

tools.name: redo
tools.description: Redo the next edit. Errors with NothingToRedo if no redo is available. A new commit truncates the redo tail.

inputSchema.title: EmptyArgs

tools.name: lock_history
tools.description: Block the user from reverting (undo / redo / restore_checkpoint) while the agent is mid-batch. `reason` is shown next to the lock badge in the record-panel header and as the error returned to revert attempts. Last-writer-wins. Always pair with an unlock_history call; releases also happen on workspace change and on user-side agent-mode exit.

reason.description: Short free-text label shown to the user while the lock is held ("applying transitions", "rendering preview", etc.). Required.

tools.name: unlock_history
tools.description: Release the revert-lock taken by lock_history. Idempotent — calling while already unlocked is a no-op.

inputSchema.title: EmptyArgs

tools.name: checkpoint
tools.description: Create an explicit named checkpoint of the current state. Checkpoints survive new commits (they don't get truncated like the redo tail) and persist in the .vproj save file. Returns the new checkpoint id. The human's agent-mode record panel renders each created checkpoint as a pin-style row with a Restore button — use this at logical batch boundaries.

tools.name: list_checkpoints
tools.description: List all named checkpoints, oldest first. Returns id, label, actor, created_at per checkpoint (no project snapshot).

inputSchema.description: Empty arg shape for tools that take no parameters. The dispatch table deserializes `{}` (or any object) into this; `schemars` advertises it as an empty object schema.
inputSchema.title: EmptyArgs

tools.name: restore_checkpoint
tools.description: Restore a named checkpoint. Records a new history entry — undo will return to the pre-restore state. Errors with CheckpointNotFound if the id doesn't exist. The agent-mode record panel prunes the rolled-back agent actions from view; a small '↩ Restored to <label>' row marks the boundary.

tools.name: dry_run
tools.description: Try-run a sequence of edit operations against a clone of the current project WITHOUT committing. Useful for previewing complex multi-step edits — agents can detect overlap / invariant violations before mutating real state. Validates after each op (matching real `commit()` behaviour) and HALTS at the first error so subsequent ops don't dry-run against a state real execution wouldn't reach. Returns `{ results: [{ index, status, output? | error? }, ...] }`. Supports add_color_layer, add_video_layer, update_layer, update_layer_params, move_layer, split_layer, delete_layer. Other tools (motifs, caption import, media import, undo/redo) are not dry-runnable in v1.

AudioRole.description: Fixed v1 role set. Custom / sub-roles are deferred. Kebab-case on the wire (matches `TrackRole`'s convention and the TS `AudioRole` union).

LayerParamsPatch.description:
Kind-tagged partial update for a layer's `params`. Fields are scalar so the UI can drive them with simple inputs; the actor lifts them to `Animated::Static(...)` where the underlying shape is animated.

Limitation: applying a static-value patch to a keyframed field overwrites the keyframe track. Acceptable for the MVP property panel where keyframes are not yet user-editable; revisit when the keyframe UI lands.

motif_id.description: Retarget the layer to a different Motif id (Edit-in-place: swap the selected layer onto a working draft; Discard: swap it back). Paired with `motif_version` so the seen-at marker matches the new target.

props.description: Props to merge into the layer's existing `props` map, FIELD-WISE — each key present here overwrites that key, all other keys are left intact. (Replacing the whole map would let a stale debounced commit clobber a concurrent edit; merge can't delete keys, which is fine — the schema keys are fixed at insert time.) No schema validation here: the actor has no motif-registry access, and props were already validated against the manifest's `props_schema` at `add_motif`.

LayerPatch.description: Partial update for a layer's envelope. Only `Some(_)` fields are applied. `params_patch` carries kind-specific edits; the property panel sends one of the variant patches so the actor can sanity-check the kind matches.

OperationSpec.description: Tagged-union mirror of the small set of mutation MCP tools that can be dry-run safely. Variants stay flat (no nested action/payload split) so the JSON shape is `{"kind": "add_color_layer", "track_id": ..., ...}`.

oneOf.description: Equivalent to the `update_layer` tool — envelope only (label / time range / enabled / locked).

operations.description: Operations to apply in order against a CLONE of current project state. First error halts the chain. Each op uses string UUIDs at the MCP boundary; the actor parses them server-side.

tools.name: set_role_gain
tools.description: Set an audio role's mix gain (dB). role ∈ {dialogue,music,sfx,voiceover}. Recorded (undoable). Folds into every layer of that role at mix time.

AudioRole.description: Fixed v1 role set. Custom / sub-roles are deferred. Kebab-case on the wire (matches `TrackRole`'s convention and the TS `AudioRole` union).

gain_db.description: Mix-bus gain in decibels. 0.0 = unity; typical range -60..+12. Sets the role's gain absolutely (replaces the current value, not additive).

tools.name: set_role_flags
tools.description: Mute/solo an audio role. role ∈ {dialogue,music,sfx,voiceover}. Unrecorded (not undoable). Mute wins over solo; any solo silences non-soloed roles.

AudioRole.description: Fixed v1 role set. Custom / sub-roles are deferred. Kebab-case on the wire (matches `TrackRole`'s convention and the TS `AudioRole` union).

tools.name: transcribe_clip
tools.description: Transcribe a VideoClip or Audio layer through the configured cloud transcription provider (OpenAI Whisper today) and return the SRT body with timestamps already shifted to timeline-absolute microseconds. Pipe the returned body straight into `apply_subtitles` (the cues self-position into a new caption track via their internal timestamps — `apply_subtitles` takes no start/end). Optional `t_start_us`/`t_end_us` narrow the transcription window inside the layer's time range; both default to the layer endpoints. VideoClip layers with speed != 1.0 are rejected — split off a speed-1 segment first. Errors with structured messages if no API key is configured, the audio slice exceeds the provider cap (~13 min for Whisper at 25 MB), or the provider rate-limits / rejects auth.

language.description: Optional ISO-639-1 language hint (`"en"`, `"zh"`). Auto-detect when omitted.

layer_id.description: Target VideoClip or Audio layer id.

t_end_us.description: Optional transcription window end in timeline microseconds. Defaults to the layer's `t_end_us`. Must lie within the layer.

t_start_us.description: Optional transcription window start in timeline microseconds. Defaults to the layer's `t_start_us`. Must lie within the layer.

tools.name: synthesize_speech
tools.description: Synthesize speech via the configured cloud TTS provider (OpenAI tts-1 today) and attach the result as an Audio layer. The MP3 is content-addressed in cache by `(model, voice, speed, text)`, so a repeat call with the same args reuses the cached file without burning another API request. Args: `text` (≤4096 chars for tts-1), `voice` (one of alloy/echo/fable/onyx/nova/shimmer), optional `speed` (0.25..4.0; default = provider default ≈1.0), optional `target_track_id` (defaults to first existing Audio track or a new 'Voiceover' track), optional `t_start_us` (defaults to the composition's current duration so the voiceover appends at the end). Returns `{ layer_id, media_id, t_start_us, t_end_us, cached }`.

speed.description: 0.25..4.0 for tts-1. Omit to use the provider default (~1.0).

t_start_us.description: Optional timeline start in microseconds. Defaults to the composition's current `duration_us` so the voiceover appends at the end.

target_track_id.description: Optional Audio track id. If omitted, lands on the first existing Audio track or auto-creates one labeled "Voiceover".

text.description: Text to synthesize. tts-1 caps at 4096 characters.

voice.description: Voice identifier. tts-1 accepts: alloy, echo, fable, onyx, nova, shimmer.

tools.name: list_motifs
tools.description: List every motif available to add via `add_motif` — built-ins PLUS installed and draft user motifs. Returns an array of `{ id, name, version, size: [w,h], default_duration_s, props_schema, status, content_hash, target_id? }` where `status` is `builtin` | `installed` | `draft`. Inspect `props_schema` before `add_motif` to know what keys + types each motif accepts; unknown keys reject. Drafts (status `draft`) are placeable immediately for preview.

inputSchema.description: Empty arg shape for tools that take no parameters. The dispatch table deserializes `{}` (or any object) into this; `schemars` advertises it as an empty object schema.
inputSchema.title: EmptyArgs

tools.name: get_motif_source
tools.description: Read a Motif's source { manifest, html } — any built-in, installed, or draft. Read this before editing so you can base your changes on the current source. `id` comes from `list_motifs`.

tools.name: write_motif_draft
tools.description: Write a Motif draft from { manifest, html }. Returns the draft id. The draft is placeable immediately (via `add_motif`) for preview, and re-writable. `from` (optional) records an existing Motif id as the draft's UPDATE target so a later `install_motif {mode:'update'}` republishes over it; omit `from` for a brand-new Motif (installs as new). The manifest's `id`/`version` are ignored — app-assigned. Expose tweakable controls via `props_schema`.

from.description: Optional id of an existing Motif this draft will UPDATE on install (records it as the draft's target). Omit for a brand-new Motif (installs as new).

html.description: The HTML body. The manifest island is injected by the app; a `<script>motif.define({...})</script>` drives the render.

manifest.description: The manifest as a JSON object (its `id`/`version` are ignored — app-assigned). Shape: `{ name, size:[w,h], default_duration_s, props_schema, ... }` — inspect a built-in via `get_motif_source` for an exact example. Rejected if malformed.

tools.name: preview_motif_draft
tools.description: Render one frame of a Motif (draft / installed / built-in) and return it as a base64-encoded PNG, so you can SEE your output and self-correct. Args: `id`, `t_sec` (content time), optional `width`/`height` (default = the motif's size), optional `props`. Requires the app's preview runtime to be live; returns an error (rather than hanging) if it isn't ready.

height.description: Optional render height (default = the motif's manifest height).

props.description: Optional props (JSON object); defaults to the manifest defaults.

t_sec.description: Content time in seconds to render (e.g. 0 = first frame).

width.description: Optional render width (default = the motif's manifest width).

tools.name: install_motif
tools.description: Install a draft. mode 'new' publishes under the draft's own id; 'update' republishes over the draft's recorded UPDATE target (set via `write_motif_draft`'s `from`) — bumping its version so every placement re-renders, and rebinding + migrating current-project layers. Returns the published id.

mode.description: "new" (publish under the draft's own id) or "update" (republish over the draft's recorded target; fails if the draft has no target).

tools.name: delete_motif
tools.description: Delete an installed or draft user Motif by id. Built-ins are rejected. Placed layers referencing it degrade to an error placeholder.

tools.name: add_motif
tools.description: Add a motif layer to a track. The motif is rasterized to a PNG sequence on first render and cached content-addressably; subsequent renders are folder lookups. Args: `motif_id` (from `list_motifs`), `t_start_us` (timeline microseconds), optional `t_end_us` (defaults to `t_start_us + default_duration_s * 1e6`), optional `track_id` (when omitted, always spawns a fresh track labeled 'Overlay' — never reuses an existing track, so consecutive auto-inserts can't collide), optional `props` (JSON object matched against the motif's `props_schema`; unknown keys reject, missing keys fall back to defaults). Returns the new layer id.

props.description: Motif props as a JSON object. Keys must match the motif's `props_schema`; unknown keys reject; missing keys fill from defaults.

t_end_us.description: Layer end in timeline microseconds. Defaults to `t_start_us + default_duration_s * 1_000_000` when omitted.

track_id.description: Target track id. If omitted, a fresh track labeled "Overlay" is created.

resources.name: Current project
resources.description: The full open WeftCut project as JSON. Re-fetch after change events.

resources.name: Composition
resources.description: Canvas size, fps, sample rate, color space, background.

resources.name: Media pool
resources.description: All imported media items keyed by id.

resources.name: Tracks
resources.description: Tracks with layer envelopes. Read project://layers/{id} for full layer detail.

resources.name: History
resources.description: Recent operations and named checkpoints (no snapshots).

resources.name: Audio mix plan
resources.description: Compiled export-audio mix plan (layer placement on the 48 kHz frame grid + envelope summaries) — for agents that want structural reasoning about what export will mix.

resources.name: Audio meter
resources.description: Latest preview master-bus level reading (rms/peak dBFS). `live: false` when nothing has played in the last 2 seconds.

resources.name: Motif catalog
resources.description: Built-in, installed, and draft Motifs (html stripped). Re-fetch after motifs:changed events.

prompts.name: cut-silences
prompts.description: Find silent regions in a clip and tighten it up by splitting + deleting the dead air.

arguments.name: layer_id
arguments.description: Target VideoClip or Audio layer id.

arguments.name: threshold_amp
arguments.description: Peak amplitude threshold in [0.0, 1.0]. Default 0.02 (≈ -34 dBFS).

arguments.name: min_silence_us
arguments.description: Minimum silence duration to cut, in microseconds. Default 500000 (0.5s).

prompts.name: auto-caption
prompts.description: Transcribe a video or audio layer with cloud Whisper, then apply the SRT as subtitles.

arguments.name: layer_id
arguments.description: Target VideoClip or Audio layer id.

arguments.name: language
arguments.description: Optional ISO-639-1 language hint (en, zh, etc.). Auto-detect when omitted.

prompts.name: voiceover
prompts.description: Generate cloud TTS for a script and attach it as an Audio layer.

arguments.name: script
arguments.description: Text to speak. tts-1 caps a single call at 4096 chars; for longer scripts split into paragraphs.

arguments.name: voice
arguments.description: OpenAI voice: alloy, echo, fable, onyx, nova, or shimmer.

arguments.name: speed
arguments.description: Optional speech speed in [0.25, 4.0]. Omit for the provider default.

arguments.name: target_track_id
arguments.description: Optional Audio track id. Defaults to the first existing Audio track or a new 'Voiceover' track.
